subject: MedArc - post-demo: ephemeral logs & 0-retention paths
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Thompson <ella@medarc.com>, security@medarc.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: MedArc demo recap + next steps on data handling

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the honest questions on PHI handling and retention. Short recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Call highlights:
- You liked the session routing + model fallback demo; key ask was strict control over any persisted prompt/response data when PHI is present.
- Security asked whether we can provide a 0-retention / session-only mode for production traffic and a shortened logs alternative for debug.
- Legal asked for a DPA clause and evidence of limited logs (SOC2 excerpts, example retention config).

What we propose (engineer + legal + PM alignment):
1) Session-only mode (ephemeral): requests containing an explicit header or workspace flag would not persist full prompts/responses to long-term logs; only ephemeral KV used for inference and transient cache.
2) Shortened logs: for customers who need debug traces, we can persist metadata and hashed artifacts (SHA-256 of prompt), redacted text, and a configurable TTL (7 days default, can be lowered).
3) Audit sampling: instead of full audit logs, we can provide a sampled audit stream for compliance review plus summary metrics.

Attachments: call notes, architecture sketch, and initial DPA draft.

Next steps I suggest:
- Ben: confirm technical feasibility and list of env flags + impact on latency/cost (ETA 2 business days).
- Rishi: note CS path and what a pilot would look like (ETA 1 week).
- Ella/EllA security: send any minimum required evidence items (SOC2, penetration test window, specific retention TTL).
- Legal: we'll push the proposed DPA clause and highlight the 0-retention mechanism for review.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short sync if that helps.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0188

From: Ella Thompson <ella@medarc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medarc.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 18:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedArc demo recap + next steps on data handling

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) "0-retention" is a hard requirement for any request that includes PHI (e.g., patient name, MRN) — that means no full-text or structured prompt/response storage outside strict ephemeral memory used for the live inference. We understand sampled telemetry for platform health is OK as long as it is aggregated and cannot be reconstituted.

2) For debug only: we would accept hashed prompt artifacts + redacted snippets if they are inaccessible to humans (hashed+salted, truncated to 128 bits) and TTL'd to <= 7 days.

3) Residency: our production workloads MUST run in a US region. Please confirm all storage telemetry adheres to US-only residency for this account.

Can Ben and Rishi call out which pieces are immediate config (no contract change) versus those requiring a formal DPA amendment / exception? Also, please include any performance impact for session-only mode.

—
Ella Thompson
Head of Platform, MedArc Health
ella@medarc.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Thompson <ella@medarc.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedArc demo recap + next steps on data handling

On Wed, Dec 9, 2026 at 6:00 PM Ella Thompson <ella@medarc.com> wrote:
> 1) "0-retention" is a hard requirement for any request that includes PHI ...

Quick technical primer / constraints:
- Feasible: We already support an "ephemeral mode" flag in the runtime for certain customers; toggling it prevents writes to long-term logs and disables KV persistence beyond the request lifetime. This is a config change and can be scoped per workspace. No code change required for the basic path.
- Debug traces: We can emit hashed artifacts and redacted snippets. Recommendation: use HMAC-SHA256 with a customer-scoped seed (so hashes cannot be correlated across tenants). We'll truncate to 128 bits for storage savings. TTL can be configured by policy; default 7d.
- Residency: we can pin telemetry and any persisted artifacts to US-only storage buckets. Need legal signoff on where the HMAC seed is stored (customer-specific or Redwood-managed HSM).
- Performance: ephemeral mode has negligible latency impact for standard conversational traffic; enabling additional redaction/hashing in the write path adds ~5-12ms per request on p50 depending on model size. Batching reduces per-token overhead.

Action items (technical):
- I'll produce a short config doc showing the workspace flag names, example headers, and expected latency delta (ETA Tue, 2026-12-14).
- Need to confirm HSM/KMS requirement for HMAC seed with security@medarc.com and legal.

—
Ben Carter
Privacy Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Ella Thompson <ella@medarc.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medarc.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedArc demo recap + next steps on data handling

Appreciate the breakdown, Ben. A couple of follow-ups from our security/legal team after an internal review: 

- Legal wants explicit language in the DPA that when the "ephemeral" flag is used, Redwood does not retain any human-readable prompts/responses and does not permit reconstitution of content from telemetry.
- Security prefers the HMAC seed be customer-provided or stored in a customer-controlled KMS/HSM. If Redwood-managed HSM is the only option, we need a contractual guarantee around access controls and rotation.
- For initial pilot we can accept 7d TTL for debug artifacts, but long term we want the ability to lower to 0 days on trigger (e.g., production PHI workflows).

We'd like a short pilot: route a non-prod workspace with the ephemeral flag on and a 7d TTL for debug artifacts, run synthetic traffic for 2 weeks, and then evaluate. If that goes well, we'll request contract language for per-workspace 0-retention on PHI-tagged traffic.

Please confirm next steps and who from Redwood legal will shepherd the DPA amendments.

—
Ella Thompson
Head of Platform, MedArc Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Thanks all — consolidating and owning the pilot coordination from CS side. TL;DR of plan we can execute quickly: 

1) Pilot scope (owner: Rishi / CS)
- Non-prod workspace configured with ephemeral=true
- Debug artifacts: hashed+truncated, TTL=7d
- US-only storage enforced
- Duration: 2 weeks synthetic + 1 week customer QA (total 3 weeks)

2) Deliverables (timeline)
- Ben: config doc + latency notes + sample redaction + seed storage options (ETA 2026-12-14)
- Legal: I'll loop in our legal contact (name: Priya Natarajan) to draft the DPA amendment language clarifying ephemeral behavior and restrictions on reconstitution (ETA 1 week to initial draft).
- Security@MedArc: please send the minimum evidence list (SOC2 scoping, pentest summary) so we can attach to the pilot packet.

3) Meeting: propose a 30-min kickoff on Monday 2026-12-15 at 10am PT to finalize test accounts and acceptance criteria.

If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and pilot runbook. Thanks Marissa for driving this.
